dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Welcome! Do you have a reservation?

glosses.meaning: a plan that keeps a room or table for you

dialogue.en: Hello! Did you ask us to keep a room?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, a room for two nights under Lee.

glosses.meaning: a part of a building with walls

dialogue.en: Yes, a room for two nights for Lee.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes, I see it. Breakfast is included.
dialogue.en: Yes, I found it. The first meal is part of the price.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Is the room available now?

glosses.meaning: a part of a building with walls

dialogue.en: Good. Can I use the room now?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Yes, it is. Here is your key. It is room 305.

glosses.meaning: a part of a building with walls
something you use to open a door

dialogue.en: Yes. This is your key. It is room 305.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. We will stay here for two nights.

glosses.meaning: to be in a place for some time

dialogue.en: Thanks. We will be here for two nights.

practice_words.tip: Say rez-er-VAY-shun: stress the third part
Say uh-VAY-luh-bul: stress the second part
